 Key points
 Domestic LPG is sold at the non-subsidised price, with the subsidy credited separately to the consumer's bank account under PAHAL, the Petroleum Ministry told the Rajya Sabha in August 2025. 
 Most transfers are completed within two days of delivery and are confirmed by SMS; a failed transfer is also reported by SMS with the corrective step. 
 As on 1 July 2025, 92.44% of 33.05 crore active consumers had Aadhaar seeded, while around 86.78% of 30.63 crore DBTL consumers are 'Aadhaar Transfer Compliant'. 
 Complaints were received on only around 0.08% of the about 194 crore refills delivered in 2024-25, mostly related to subsidy transfer or delivery delays. 
 Advertisement
 Most LPG subsidy credits reach a domestic consumer’s bank account within two days of delivery, the Petroleum Ministry told the Rajya Sabha in August 2025, with the cylinder sold at the non-subsidised price under PAHAL.
 “Once the subsidy is credited, the consumer receives an SMS confirming the subsidy deposit,” the Ministry said in its written reply to a Starred Question. If the transfer fails, the consumer is told of the issue and the corrective action to take, also by SMS.
 The reply does not state how much the subsidy is for each cylinder.
 Complaints on 0.08% of refills
 The Ministry’s own count for 2024-25 shows about 194 crore LPG refills delivered, with complaints on around 0.08% of them — mostly related to subsidy transfer or delivery delays. On our arithmetic, that 0.08% works out to about 15.5 lakh refills.
 Why a transfer can fail
 When a transfer does not go through, the causes are on the bank or Aadhaar side rather than the gas company’s. The Ministry listed deseeding of Aadhaar from bank accounts, bank mergers, inactive Aadhaar numbers, and account closures or transfers as the causes.
 The reply gives two separate figures for Aadhaar readiness. As on 1 July 2025, 92.44% of a total 33.05 crore active LPG consumers had their Aadhaar seeded in the oil companies’ database, while around 86.78% of the total 30.63 crore DBTL consumers were “Aadhaar Transfer Compliant”. The Government had also directed public sector oil companies to undertake and complete biometric Aadhaar authentication of PMUY and PAHAL beneficiaries.
 The three SMS at every refill, and the delivery code
 A consumer gets an SMS at three points — when the refill is booked, when the cash memo is generated, and when the cylinder is delivered — so a wrong or missed delivery can be tracked and reported, the Ministry said. The cash-memo SMS also carries a Delivery Authentication Code, which has to be shared with the delivery personnel at the time of delivery.
 Where to complain
 A consumer who sees no credit SMS, or wants to report a delivery problem, can call the toll-free helpline 1800 2333 555, use the oil companies’ websites, apps, chatbots, WhatsApp or social media pages, file on CPGRAMS or MoPNGeSEVA, or go to the distributor’s office directly. A separate number, 1906, is for an LPG leak or accident.
 Who this reply is about
 The scheme covers domestic LPG connections only. Within domestic consumers, the targeted subsidy is aimed at Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) beneficiaries, who must also clear a biometric Aadhaar check — done for 67% of existing PMUY beneficiaries as on 1 July 2025, and required for every new consumer before the connection is released, the Ministry said.
 The Ministry has also been removing connections it counts as duplicate or inactive: 4.08 crore duplicate, fake or inactive LPG connections were blocked, suspended or deactivated as on 1 July 2025, and 8.49 lakh PMUY connections have been terminated since inception after de-duplication exercises. Separately, around 12,000 inactive PMUY connections have been terminated under a January 2025 standard operating procedure for PMUY consumers who had not taken any refills after installation of their connection.
 LPG distribution is regulated through the Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Supply and Distribution) Order, 2000, and the oil companies’ Marketing Discipline Guidelines, which provide for penal action against distributors found indulging in malpractice.
 A third-party evaluation by the Research and Development Initiative, cited in the reply, found more than 90% of respondents satisfied with the subsidy reimbursement mechanism, and recommended improving targeting by limiting subsidies to economically weaker sections.
 PAHAL, under which the subsidy is paid this way, has been implemented since January 2015.
 Source: Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, PIB press release ‘Government Strengthens LPG Subsidy Transfers Through PAHAL and Aadhaar Authentication: Petroleum Minister Hardeep S Puri’ (Release ID 2152413), 5 August 2025.

 Critical AdSense behaviour: adsbygoogle.push({}) does NOT bind to
 a specific . It says "process the next unbound in DOM
 order." So if you push N times, AdSense binds the first N 
 slots it finds.
 Live investigation (2026-05-29) showed the right sidebar still
 loading late on indianpaycalculator.in. DOM order of :
 1. LEFT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-left)
 2-5. Display banners (4× AdBanner inside page content)
 6. RIGHT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-right, after main slot)
 7. Mobile anchor (StickyAnchorAd at body end)
 Previously this script pushed twice (one per sidebar). Those 2
 pushes bound LEFT + Display#1, NOT LEFT + RIGHT. The other 5
 slots only got bound as AdBanner.client:visible islands hydrated
 on scroll — meaning the right sidebar was bound 6th, after the
 user scrolled past every in-page banner. That's the "right side
 opens very late" complaint.
 Fix: push once per SSR'd ad slot. AdSense binds them all in DOM
 order at body parse end — no React hydration wait, no scroll-to-
 view wait. Subsequent React useEffect pushes (from AdUnit /
 StickyAnchorAd) become no-ops since the AdUnit effect skips when
 data-adsbygoogle-status is already set. --> component was removed 2026-05-29 to eliminate the
 duplicate-anchor conflict where both the manual slot 4961033893 and
 Auto Anchor would compete on mobile, causing one to fail to fill. -->
